Extend the ProductCatalog cache with a stale-data policy. Existing callers must continue to get strict behavior by default. Concurrency is out of scope.

Add public enum FreshnessPolicy { RequireFresh, AllowStaleOnTransientFailure } and public sealed record CatalogValue(string Value, bool IsStale). Add public CatalogValue CatalogCache.Read(string key, FreshnessPolicy policy). Reject an undefined policy with ArgumentOutOfRangeException before calling the loader. CatalogCache.Get(string key) still behaves like RequireFresh and returns the string.

A cache entry is fresh when its age is less than 30 seconds. Return fresh data without loading in either policy and mark IsStale false. At age 30 seconds or later, attempt to refresh. A successful refresh resets the age from completion of that load and returns IsStale false. Only when a refresh throws CatalogUnavailableException, policy is AllowStaleOnTransientFailure, and the previous entry's age is still less than 90 seconds when the loader throws, return that entry with IsStale true. This fallback does not reset the age or skip the next refresh attempt. Missing, invalidated, cleared, and 90-second-old entries are ineligible. Other exceptions always propagate. Get, Invalidate, and Clear retain their signatures.

Add public bool IsStale { get; init; } to CardReadResult, preserving its existing primary constructor and deconstruction. Add public IReadOnlyList<CardReadResult> ProductCardReader.ReadMany(IEnumerable<string?> keys, FreshnessPolicy policy), retaining the one-argument overload as strict. Validate unknown policies before enumerating keys. All prior ordering, trimming, sharing, and per-key error rules remain. A stale fallback is a success with IsStale true. Errors and fresh successes have IsStale false. Every duplicate occurrence must get the same IsStale and description or error as the first occurrence in that call. ProductCardReader.Read remains strict.

Keep the library buildable without external packages.
